chapter: Buddy Petit and Sam Morgan years
title: Who played in Buddy Petit's band at Economy Hall
summary: Williams lists Buddy Petit's sidemen (Manaday, Zeb Lenares, Simon on bass) and struggles to place the trombonist.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Pajot played out there too. Mm-hmm. He had a band out there. But not with Henry Martin, a different time? No, I don't think, I don't think. No. No. Because that was before Pajot's time, you know, see, I imagine. Oh yeah. What about Buddy Petit? Did you remember who played with him much?

Well, when I was playing with him, we had Buddy Petit, and we had all trombone with us. We had Buddy Manatee, we had Zeb Lennaris, and we had Simon the Wild on bass. And he had clarinet, and Zeb Lennaris on clarinet, on trombone. Morris Francis with a René in attire. I can picture the band on the bandstand in the Economy Hall. Hmm. But I can't picture the trombone playing.
And who'd you say was a guitar player, a banjo player? Buddy Manatee. Buddy Manatee and Simon. And Simon. And no piano, of course. No. No violin. No. No.

Now that trombone, I can't place where it was. It might have been yanked. It might have been. I'm not sure. Yanked Johnson. Uh-huh. Trying to see who else was the nice trombone player on at that time. I know he had George Washington later. Oh, yeah. He was out way later. That way. I can't picture who that was. No. No. He never even used Joe. He couldn't play, you know.
Joe played with one joe. No. He couldn't play, you know.
But he didn't play with the real popular bands, Joe.
No. Me neither. That's what I'm saying. That's what I used to get after Kim, man. I ain't used to playing with them kind of fellas. I mean, no.
I thought Mealy played with Chris and Buddy and some of the fans.

He didn't play with Buddy when I was playing with him. Yeah. No, indeed. No. He might have played with Chris Kelly. He might have. He might have played with Chris, because there wasn't too much to Chris. He was kind of popular, you know. Never had no kind of band. He ain't happy playing with him once. He had a pretty, fair band.
Coach Happy. The Red Happy. I can't picture that trombone player.

I can see the cooperators, cooperators, all, and economy all. I can see ourselves sitting there playing, but now who's that trombone? I can't remember. Another one, Morris Frankel, he was playing with René at the time. When I was playing with Buddy Petit, how come to play with Sam Morgan, Buddy Petit had Manny Gabriel.
